title: Sociocultural Approach Adventure 3: Culture & Conformity
welcome_lead: Today you'll explore Hofstede's cultural dimensions and Asch's conformity studies.
meta_desc: Psychology Sociocultural: Hofstede cultural dimensions, Asch conformity, enculturation and acculturation.
final_note: You linked culture to conformity, encul-turation and acculturation.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Geert Hofstede (1980 IBM study) ranked national cultures on six dimensions.

Key for psychology: individualism vs collectivism, power distance, uncertainty avoidance, long-term orientation.

Individualist cultures stress autonomy and personal achievement; collectivist stress harmony and group goals.

Solomon Asch (1951) used a line-judgement task with confederates giving the wrong answer.

On 32% of trials, participants conformed to the obvious wrong; 75% conformed at least once.

Berry (1967) replicated cross-culturally: conformity was higher in collectivist (Temne) than individualist (Inuit) samples.

Enculturation — growing up in one's own culture, internalising its norms.

Acculturation (Berry 1997): adjusting to a second culture. Four strategies: integration, assimilation, separation, marginalisation.

Acculturative stress is highest for marginalisation and lowest for integration.
